title: Recursive Accelerating Return: A Generative Collapse Dynamics Theory of Endogenous Generative Capacity
source_native_claims: Recursive Accelerating Return (RAR) is formulated as a derived regime of Generative Collapse Dynamics; it does not redefine the Tier-1 UMCP kernel (source-stated publication status).

The claim is conditional: if structure survives collapse, returns admissibly, alters the next generator under a declared equivalence rule, has a positive identified effect on later productive capacity, and the positive log-gain per unit elapsed inter-return time increases across successive admissible returns, then the trajectory belongs to a RAR solution class of GCD.
Showing that inheritance caused the rate increase requires an additional longitudinal counterfactual; the classification does not by itself establish causal RAR.

The study-level contract GCD.RAR.CORE freezes the cycle boundary, admissible return domain, canonical return test, inter-return interval rule, capacity functional, resource normalization, operator-equivalence rule, causal capacity test, model-comparison rule, uncertainty policy, and any exogenous-exposure policy; a domain implementation must additionally declare a Tier-2 mapping contract GCD.RAR.MAP.<domain>.
Evidence boundary (source-stated): formal theory, synthetic operational demonstrations, and a prospective falsification design are included; no empirical validation of RAR is claimed.
